newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao denied regular bail in forgery case.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao denied regular bail in forgery case.

text.p: A New Delhi court dismissed on Tuesday a regular bail plea by former Indian prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a forgery case and gave him until November 14 to appeal to a higher court.
Immediately after the hearing by metropolitan magistrate Prem Kumar, Rao's lawyer R.K. Anand told reporters: "He is appealing against this order in a sessions court today."

Kumar's ruling was for regular bail. Rao, 75, had so-called anticipatory, or temporary, bail, which had been due to expire on Wednesday. If denied bail by a higher court by November 14, Rao could be arrested and taken into custody.

Rao, who resigned as prime minister after his Congress party was defeated in general elections in April and May, appeared in the court twice last week for bail hearings in the seven-year- old case of alleged criminal forgery.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), India's federal police, on September 26 charged Rao and three others with involvement in an alleged attempt in 1989 to defame V.P. Singh, a Congress rebel who later became prime minister.
They are alleged to have forged documents which aimed to show Singh's son held $21 million in a bank account on the Caribbean island of St Kitts. Rao has not commented publicly on the case.
